cards.explanation: The answer is that God does not exist, friends. The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." (Psalm 14:1) Notice where he says it: in his heart. David doesn't dress it up. He just calls the one who says it the fool.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, "There is no one who does good." (Psalm 14:1) David doesn't leave a few folks out there doing good. He says it flat out, and he comes back to it in verse 3.

The answer is anyone who understands and seeks God, friends. The LORD looks down "…to see if any understand, if any seek God." (Psalm 14:2) Notice what He's looking for. It isn't muscle or presents. It's someone who understands and seeks Him.

The answer is all, friends. "All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one." (Psalm 14:3) Not most. Not nearly everybody. David says all, then adds "…not even one." so nobody sneaks out the side door.

The answer is that they refuse to call upon the LORD, friends. The psalm says, "They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon the LORD." (Psalm 14:4) It's one thing to do harm. It's another to refuse to even call on Him. The psalm asks if they will never learn.

The answer is that God is in the company of the righteous, friends. The psalm says, "There they are, overwhelmed with dread, for God is in the company of the righteous." (Psalm 14:5) The "for" gives the reason right there in the verse. God is in the company of the righteous, and that's what has them overwhelmed with dread.

The answer is True, friends, and I love this verse. "You sinners frustrate the plans of the oppressed, yet the LORD is their shelter." (Psalm 14:6) See that "yet"? Even with their plans being frustrated, the LORD is still their shelter.

The answer is salvation coming from Zion, friends. "Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion!" (Psalm 14:7) David is longing for it. It's an "Oh, that…" kind of wish, the kind that comes from the heart.

The answer is joy, friends. "When the LORD restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!" (Psalm 14:7) Rejoicing and gladness are joy, plain and simple. After all that heavy stuff, the psalm ends with a happy shout.
